title: Cockcroft Gault
description: Estimates creatinine clearance (CrCl) for medication dosing using the Cockcroft-Gault equation.

faq.question: When should I use Cockcroft-Gault instead of CKD-EPI?
faq.answer: Use Cockcroft-Gault when adjusting medication doses, as many drug labels still reference CrCl from this equation.

faq.question: What weight should I use in the Cockcroft-Gault equation?
faq.answer: Use actual body weight by default. Adjusted body weight may be used in obese patients per institutional guidelines.

advice: Use actual body weight unless adjusted body weight is clinically indicated (e.g. obesity).
Cockcroft-Gault remains the preferred equation for many drug dosing recommendations.
Use stable serum creatinine; avoid using values during acute kidney injury for chronic dosing.
warnings: Not recommended for unstable kidney function or acute kidney injury.
Overestimates creatinine clearance in elderly patients with low muscle mass.
Does not provide direct GFR estimation; use CKD-EPI for CKD staging.
followUp: Verify drug-specific dosing guidelines for renal adjustment thresholds.
Monitor renal function periodically in patients with CrCl < 50 mL/min.
